semanticAnalysis.sprintSummary: This sprint appears to have two parallel workstreams: developing new application features for content and proposal management, and a significant effort focused on producing marketing videos for YouTube. A large number of tasks are dedicated to non-engineering activities like video production, learning platform basics, and administrative steps, rather than building or maintaining software.

problematicTasks.title: Write Video Script
issues: This is a marketing or content creation task, not software engineering.
Excessively granular; should be part of a larger epic for content production.

problematicTasks.title: Learn YouTube Studio
issues: Learning is an activity, not a deliverable or a task.
Tracking learning as a task suggests either a fundamental skill gap for the role or an attempt to pad sprint velocity with non-productive work.

problematicTasks.title: Learn Video Quality Review Process
issues: Learning is an activity, not a deliverable.
This is not a software engineering task.

problematicTasks.title: Learn YouTube SEO Fundamentals. Learn Thumbnail Review Best Practices
issues: Learning is not a task with a deliverable.
This is a marketing skill, not an engineering one.

problematicTasks.title: Learn YouTube Analytics, Perform Channel Review and Monitoring
issues: Combines a non-task ('Learn') with a vague ongoing activity ('Monitoring').
This is a marketing analyst function, not software engineering.

problematicTasks.title: Save Assets to Google Drive
issues: This is a trivial administrative step, not a unit of engineering work.
Should be included as a 'definition of done' criterion for the asset creation task (#2165), not a separate ticket.

problematicTasks.title: Analyze Automation Workflows, Define Application Requirements, and Review Generated App Designs
issues: Task is too broad and combines multiple distinct phases of work (analysis, requirements definition, design review).
Each clause in the title could be its own epic or large task.

duplicateOrOverlapping.reason: These are all sequential micro-tasks for a single logical outcome: 'Produce and Publish Demo Video'. They should be consolidated into one or at most two tasks.
These tasks represent a single research effort: 'Research YouTube best practices and report on channel strategy'. They are not individual work items.

unclearWork.title: Document Issues and Recommendations
unclearWork.problem: The scope is undefined. It is unclear what 'Issues' are being documented, for what system, and what the format or depth of 'Recommendations' should be. The deliverable is ambiguous.

unclearWork.title: Enhance and Optimize LinkedIn Post Generation Prompt for Weekly
unclearWork.problem: The terms 'Enhance' and 'Optimize' are subjective and lack measurable success criteria. A better task would define the target outcome, e.g., 'Refine LinkedIn prompt to reduce manual editing time by 25%'.

strengths: The breakdown of application feature development into specific, deliverable-oriented tasks is a strength (e.g., API setup, screen creation, functionality implementation).
Tasks like #2174 ('Setup Google Sheets API Integration') and #2179 ('Approve or Reject Content Functionality') represent clear, well-scoped engineering work.
The pattern of creating separate tasks for individual UI screens (#2176, #2177, #2185, #2186) is a good practice for organizing and tracking front-end development.
